function.description: Send a GET request to a specified URL to retrieve all products and branches with triangulation runs in the latest 90 days. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to send the GET request to.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: The MIME types that are acceptable for the response.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request as a dictionary of header names to header values.

timeout.description: The maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

days.description: The number of days to look back for triangulation runs.

end_date.description: The end date for the data retrieval period, in the format 'YYYY-MM-DD'. If null, defaults to the current date.

params.description: Optional query parameters to include in the request.

auth.description: HTTP authentication credentials as a (username, password) tuple.

cert.description: Path to a certificate file to verify the peer.

cookies.description: Cookies to send with the request as a dictionary of cookie names to cookie values.

http.description: URL of the proxy for HTTP requests.

https.description: URL of the proxy for HTTPS requests.

proxies.description: Proxy settings as a dictionary mapping protocol names to URLs of the proxies.

stream.description: If true, the response should be streamed; otherwise, the response will be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not.

message.content:
**Triangulation Metrics** refers to a set of quantitative measures used to evaluate the quality, reliability, and performance of triangulation processes—typically in contexts such as geographic information systems (GIS), computer vision, robotics, or data fusion. These metrics help determine how accurately multiple observations or sensors can be combined to infer a common point or state.

Key aspects often covered by triangulation metrics include:

| Metric | What it Measures | Typical Use |
|--------|------------------|-------------|
| **Accuracy** | Difference between the estimated position and the true position. | Assessing overall precision of the triangulation algorithm. |
| **Precision / Variance** | Spread of repeated estimates around their mean. | Evaluating consistency across multiple runs. |
| **Error Ellipse / Covariance Matrix** | Statistical representation of uncertainty in two‑dimensional space. | Visualizing confidence bounds on the estimated location. |
| **Root Mean Square Error (RMSE)** | Square root of the average squared error over many trials. | Summarizing overall error magnitude. |
| **Mean Absolute Error (MAE)** | Average absolute difference between estimate and truth. | Robust measure less sensitive to outliers. |
| **Bias** | Systematic offset from the true value. | Detecting consistent directional errors. |
| **Confidence Interval Coverage** | Proportion of times the true value falls within a calculated interval. | Checking statistical validity of uncertainty estimates. |
| **Computation Time / Complexity** | Time taken or computational resources required. | Comparing efficiency of different algorithms. |
| **Robustness to Outliers** | Sensitivity of the estimate to erroneous inputs. | Ensuring reliability under noisy conditions. |
| **Convergence Rate** | How quickly iterative methods approach the true solution. | Optimizing iterative triangulation schemes. |

In practice, a triangulation system might report several of these metrics together—for example, an RMSE of 2 m, a bias of 0.3 m, and a 95 % confidence ellipse radius of 1.5 m—providing a comprehensive picture of its performance.
